title: Reverse group-commit window: commit_delay 0, commit_siblings 5, flush_after 64
configuration_cause: commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 forces a fixed per-commit stall on nearly every commit (only 5 terminals, so 2 siblings is almost always satisfied), while wal_writer_flush_after=0 disables writer flush batching. r008 widened this window to 500us and the paired TPS effect was inconsistent (22.8%, -2.5%, -24.8%) with sync_average_ms refuted as decreasing. The window is pure added latency, not coalescing benefit.
mechanism: With only 5 client terminals, commit_delay cannot collect enough concurrent committers to amortize its fixed sleep; it adds ~100us to every commit while sync_average_ms stays ~0.10-0.14ms (fsync is already cheap, host_io stall fraction 0.0). r008's 500us window produced no consistent sync reduction and refuted the TPS gain. Reversing the group-commit window to 0 removes the per-commit stall, and setting wal_writer_flush_after=64 restores writer-side flush batching so the background writer coalesces WAL writes without gating foreground commits. commit_siblings=5 keeps the (now zero) window from ever activating.
query_effect: No plan change; commit-path latency for InsertTweet and all committing transactions drops by removing the fixed commit_delay sleep.
expected_tps_effect: Modest increase in successful_transaction_tps by freeing terminal capacity currently spent in commit_delay sleeps; effect bounded because GetUserTweets (read-only, 88% terminal capacity) does not commit.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 and overall p95 decrease slightly; GetUserTweets unaffected.

predictions.rationale: fsync is already ~0.1ms with zero host_io stalls; removing commit_delay should not change per-sync latency, only its frequency.
Removing the 100us fixed commit_delay sleep from every commit lowers InsertTweet tail latency.
Freed terminal capacity from removed commit stalls raises completed transaction throughput.

alternatives.statement: If commit_delay were genuinely coalescing fsyncs, widening it (r008) would have consistently reduced sync_average_ms and raised TPS; r008 refuted both, so the window is pure stall.

If WAL buffer capacity rather than commit gating were the bottleneck, raising wal_buffers would reduce wal_waiting_backends; but wal_buffers is already at safe high 2048 and wal_waiting_backends.max stays 1.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent carries commit_delay=100 with commit_siblings=2, a near-always-active fixed sleep that r008 showed does not buy sync coalescing. Removing it and restoring writer flush batching should recover the terminal capacity lost to commit stalls without touching the read-dominated GetUserTweets path.

nodes.label: Remove fixed per-commit stall; restore writer flush batching

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Safe low bound 0; r008 showed 500us window refuted sync reduction and inconsistent TPS, so reverse to 0 to eliminate the fixed per-commit stall.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: group-commit collection window; 0 disables the fixed sleep

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Raise from 2 to 5 within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 5 siblings means the (zero) window never activates, preventing accidental stall.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: group-commit activation threshold; high value keeps window inactive

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Set from 0 to 64 (8kB units = 512kB) within safe [0,1024]; restores writer-side flush batching so background writer coalesces WAL writes without gating foreground commits.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: writer flush batch size; batches background WAL writes
